paragraphs: Here's what jumps out at me, friend. The LORD picked Jehu, and Jehu never applied for a thing. He was sitting with the other army commanders when a young prophet showed up with a flask of oil, and the LORD's word came right to him: "I anoint you king over the LORD’s people Israel." (2 Kings 9:6) When God hands out a job, He's the one who does the choosing. I would have been sitting there like, "Me? I just came for the sitting!"

The job came with a reason, too. The LORD said the house of Ahab would be struck down to avenge "the blood of My servants the prophets and the blood of all the servants of the LORD shed by the hand of Jezebel." (2 Kings 9:7) I think this part is heavy, friend, and the LORD doesn't treat it lightly. He sees what happened to His servants, and He answers it. Nobody who belongs to Him was ever lost in the shuffle.

Now look at how the story moves. Elisha gave a plain order, "Do not delay!" (2 Kings 9:3), and the young prophet did exactly what he was told, then ran. When the LORD speaks, the right move is to listen and do it. Jehu's men heard the news and spread their garments under him, so the word got out FAST, and this story is still in the oven.
